d: Grand hall in the royal palace of Madrid. Two side doors of which the one on the right leads to the interior apartments, the one on the left to the anti-cameras. At the bottom a large gallery, which crosses the whole theater, formed by arches with windows covered by rich curtains, falling from top to bottom. Hanging on the wall a great portrait of the Queen. A table with the necessities to write, chairs etc. Don Salustio, dressed in black velvet according to the costume of the times of Charles II with gold toson to the neck and a large cloak of light velvet richly embroidered, enters from the door to the left. It is absorbed in deep thoughts looking at some flowers, which he has in his hand.
A Paggio is said, then Don Guritano old military, but dressed in exaggerated elegance.
Don Salustio alone.
Don Salustio indi Ruy Blas.
Don Pedro and Don Fernando, who enter favelando together and sayings.
An outing and sayings, then the Queen.

A room next to the Queen's bedroom. On the right is a door with a rich door. On the left is a pretty large window with glass windows up to the ground, from which you can see an external terrace. On the side of the door there is an effigy of Saint Maria Esclava, in front of which a lamp burns. On the side of the window there is a portrait of King Charles II, of life size and standing. On the front of the scene there is a very elegant table, on which is a rich drawer of ivory inlaid, some books and the need to write. Next to the table there is an armchair, and a small box. On the left side there is a larger and less adorned armchair. Before the image of the saint there is a velvet kneeler cremisi. In the middle of the scene there is a rather high gardener full of flowers of various kinds. On the bottom there is a larger door with a door. The Queen is seated on the armchair at the table intent to read a book; Casilda is sitting on the small armchair on the small armchair with flowers of various
The Queen alone.
A Duchess, Casilda, Don Guritano, the Damigelle, then Ruy Blas, in a rich squire's suit.
Ruy Blas, ind Don Guritano.
The Queen, Casilda is said.

The council room in the king's palace in Madrid. A large door in the middle, which is accessed by three steps: another door to the right; a window to the left. In a corner of the hall a small secret door hidden under the upholstery, which recuperates the walls. On the right a rather large table of four-length shape, with a green velvet carpet, on which are arranged various papers, the necessities for writing and the urn for secret scrutiny. Around the table various scans and an armchair located at one of the two ends of it. Don Pedro, Don Fernando and choir of the king's private Councillors.

Ruy Blas dressed in black velvet, with a rich mantle and white feather on the hat, and with the cross of Calatrava, appears on the middle door and stops rather to listen to the question arose between Don Pedro and Don Fernando, then slowly descends the steps and advances with noble and severe attitude in the middle of the scene. Don Pedro, Don Fernando and the Chorus mutiny in his presence.
The Queen and Ruy Blas.
Ruy Blas, indi Don Salustio, indi l'Usiere.

The throne room in the king's palace in Madrid is very sumptuously decorated. On the right is the throne raised on five steps with two rich golden armchairs and canopy of crimson velvet. On the left of the very high niches, within which are the statues of the kings of Spain, and among them that of Charles V. In the middle of the niches a large window with windows to the ground. In the bottom three large arches, which give access to a large room of arms. In the pillars, which are among the arches, other niches and other statues. On the steps of the throne, beside the armchairs destined for the king and queen some golden scans covered with velvet. Don Pedro and Don Fernando enter by talking to each other, while the scene is populated by other Grandi of Spain and Dame all richly clothed. Shortly after the Queen enters, preceded by Guardies, who deploy at the bottom; surrounded by his Damigelles, among which is Casassa and Sei; among which is Casssca, among which is the kings;

A small toilet in the private room of Don Salustio decorated sumptuously, but with severe and severe style. A door in the middle and two side. A table with the necessities to write, a few books and a bell. A rather large and beautifully golden armchair is at the table. Ruy Blas sitting at the table.
Don Guritano carrying two swords and sayings.
Casilda entering from the medium introduced by a Paggio.
Don Sallustio, the Paggio is said.
Ruy Blas, who enters the left door completely unarmed, then the Queen.
Don Sallustio and sayings.
Queen Ruy Blas.
